chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the white thread in contrast to the black thread, so he said: 'The whiteness of the day from the darkness of the night.' He said: 'And Bilal used to give the adhan for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when the dawn rose, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When you hear the voice of Bilal, then stop eating and drinking, for you have become morning (i.e., it is time to fast)."'

key_terms.الْخَيْطِ الْأَبْيَضِ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْ: The white thread in contrast to the black thread (a metaphor for the line of dawn)
key_terms.بَيَاضُ النَّهَارِ: The whiteness of the day (dawn light)
key_terms.فَقَدْ أَصْبَحْتُمْ: For you have become morning (i.e., entered the time of morning)
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنُ: To give the call to prayer (adhan)

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of dawn for starting the fast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise definition of *Al-Fajr al-Sadiq* (true dawn) as the horizontal band of whiteness distinct from the night's darkness, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for determining the start of fasting. It links this astronomical sign to the practical legal ruling (*hukm*) where the Prophet instructed companions to cease eating upon hearing Bilal’s Adhan, establishing the call to prayer as the audible marker for the onset of the fast.
